map.：纯金量 = 总重 × 千分比/1000 = 10 × 916/1000 = 9: : Fine gold content = total weight x parts per thousand/1000 = 10 x 916/1000 = 9.16 g. That is, 10 g of 22K gold contains 9.16 g of fine gold.
map.：同重 10g，Au999 纯金 9.99g、Au916 纯金 9.16g，差: : The same 10 g weight gives 9.99 g of fine gold for Au999 and 9.16 g for Au916, a difference of 0.83 g of fine gold; higher purity is softer and better suited to plain gold pieces.

map.Au 后数字是含金量千分比：Au750=75%(18K)、Au916=91.6%: The number after Au is the gold content in parts per thousand: Au750 = 75% (18K), Au916 = 91.6% (22K), Au999 = 99.9% (fine gold).

map.按总重与印记千分比计算纯金量和合金部分，并在 K 金、百分比、千分比之间换算；参: Compute fine gold and alloy from total weight and the stamped parts-per-thousand figure, and convert between karat, percentage and per-mille. The percentage and equivalent karat in the reference table are both derived from the same per-mille figure.
map.纯金量 = 总重 × 千分比 ÷ 1000；百分比 = 千分比 ÷ 10；等效: Fine gold = total weight × per-mille ÷ 1000; percentage = per-mille ÷ 10; equivalent karat = per-mille × 24 ÷ 1000. Entering 999.9‰ shows 99.99% and 24.00K, and the result note keeps 999.9‰ instead of rounding it to 1000‰.
map.：14K 按 585‰ 计，百分比为 58.50%，等效 K 为 14.04K；: : 14K is taken as 585‰, which is 58.50% and 14.04K equivalent. 999.9‰ shows 99.99% and 24.00K, and the result note keeps 999.9‰ rather than rounding to 1000‰.
The reference table uses common trade figures (14K as 585‰), which can differ from theoretical karat values by 0.1–0.2 percentage points. Recycling payment should use the assayed fineness after melting.
map.参考表的百分比和 K 值怎么算？: How are percentage and karat in the reference table calculated?
map.两者都由同一千分比推导：百分比 = 千分比 ÷ 10，等效 K = 千分比 ×: Both come from the same per-mille figure: percentage = per-mille ÷ 10 and equivalent karat = per-mille × 24 ÷ 1000. So 585‰ is consistently 58.50% and 14.04K instead of hand-written values that disagree.
map.焊点会影响纯金量吗？: Do solder joints affect fine gold content?
map.会。K 金首饰的焊点通常用低一档成色的焊料（如 14K 件用 10K 焊料），焊: Yes. Solder joints in karat jewellery usually use one grade lower (e.g. 10K solder on 14K pieces). The joint is a small share of the weight but lower in fineness. For precision, weigh the joint separately and convert at its actual fineness; for daily estimates it can be ignored (usually under 2% of total weight). Refiners pay on assayed fineness after melting, which commonly differs from the hallmark calculation by 1–3%.
